name: GT.M
tagline: FIS's high-throughput M (MUMPS) database and compiler, behind major core-banking systems.
description: GT.M is a key-value database engine and compiler for the ISO-standard M language (MUMPS), now developed by FIS. Data is stored in hierarchical globals with ACID transactions, before- and after-image journaling, and logical multi-site replication built for continuous availability. It underpins FIS Profile core banking and many VistA healthcare deployments. FIS publishes the source and Linux x86_64 builds as free software on SourceForge, with releases continuing in the V7 series. YottaDB is a more openly developed fork with extra language APIs. GT.M remains the conservative, vendor-backed choice for M workloads.

license.name: GNU AGPL v3.0 (Linux x86_64); commercial on other platforms

pricing.notes: Free on GNU/Linux x86_64; support and other platforms through FIS.

scale.notes: Logical multi-site replication keeps a standby instance current for failover.

strengths: Very high transaction throughput for M applications
Journaling and replication designed for banking-grade availability
Long-lived, vendor-maintained code base with free Linux builds
weaknesses: Tied to the M language and its small talent pool
Minimal modern language bindings compared with YottaDB
Development happens behind closed doors at FIS
useCases: FIS Profile and other M-based core-banking systems
VistA and M-based health record systems
